page: Google Cloud Platform g4-standard-24 is a graphics-optimized virtual machine configured with the x86_64 CPU architecture. This server type features 24 dedicated vCPUs and 90.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 3.75 GB per vCPU. Acceleration is provided by a fractional GPU allocation consisting of 0.5 NVIDIA RTX Pro 6000 GPU from the Ada Lovelace family, which features 48 GB of total VRAM.

This instance does not include local storage, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached volumes. There are zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses included with this configuration. The fractional GPU allocation of 0.5 units represents a resource-sharing model, which offers a cost-efficient entry point for workloads requiring GPU acceleration without the need for a full dedicated GPU card.

The hardware profile of the g4-standard-24 makes it suitable for graphics-intensive workloads, 3D rendering, virtual workstations, and moderate machine learning inference tasks. The combination of 24 dedicated vCPUs and 90.0 GB of RAM supports multi-threaded application processing alongside GPU-accelerated tasks.
